conviction_note: No usable option chain and a baseline history built from non-earnings 6-Ks, so I rebuilt the scale from the four confirmed releases (Nov-2025 +3.6%, Mar-2026 -0.4%, May-2026 +3.3%, Aug-2026 -10.2% day one and -28% over three sessions) and raised it for a near-certain guidance reset to fold in the IPS acquisition (abs 6.0). The sign is close to a coin flip: an H2 EBITDA ramp that looks steep against H1 ($28.0m done of an $85-90m year) and a market that has punished cash burn, set against ~$8.8m of CEO open-market buying around the quarter close and a depressed, uncrowded name. p_up 47. The findings sum to -1.1, which is close to the scaled -0.36.

positioning_check: Short interest 66,830 shares as of 2026-08-31, 0.2% of shares outstanding, 2.4 days to cover (MarketBeat https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/options-nayax-ltd-nasdaq-nyax-short-interest-update-2026-09-14/ ). Not crowded, so a squeeze is not a mechanism here. No options market, so there is no skew. Nasdaq turnover is thin, about 20k shares (~$1m) a day, and price discovery is shared with TASE (1175116), which is open when the bmo release lands. Spot $48.51 is 36% below the 52-week high and up 10.75% over 20 days. CEO Yair Nechmad bought about $8.8m in open-market purchases between 2026-09-24 and 2026-10-02. Sell-side: KBW upgraded to Outperform after the August fall (Globes 2026-08-16); Jefferies is Buy with a $68.30 target (2026-10-07).

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide was set before the IPS Group deal. IPS closed on 2026-10-01 and the company says it adds $20-22m of revenue and more than $5m of adj. EBITDA in Q4. H1 adj. EBITDA was $28.0m ($13.9m Q1 + $14.1m Q2), so the $85-90m guide needs $57-62m in H2: 2.0-2.2x H1, against 1.74x last year (H1 2025 ~$22.3m, H2 2025 $38.8m). Q3 also carries ~$4.5m of accelerated Brazil-amendment expense. If the release keeps $85-90m (or $510-520m) 'including IPS', the organic outlook has been cut by roughly $5m of EBITDA and $20m of revenue. A raise of about the IPS contribution (to ~$530-542m and ~$90-95m) would be neutral.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-10: revenue and EBITDA guide reaffirmed but the FCF conversion guide cut from ~40% to 5-10%. Stock -10.2% on day one (69.06 to 62.00), then -13.1% and -7.4% (Yahoo daily bars). 2025-11-12: FY2025 revenue and EBITDA guide cut on M&A timing, stock +3.6% at the close after -5.7% pre-market.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side models probably carry IPS from Q4, but nobody has published whether the company will roll it into the range or add it on top. EPS consensus of $0.15 (about Q2's adjusted level) suggests the Street is not modelling the full EBITDA ramp. If the market were sure the guide would hold organically, the stock would not sit 36% below its high a quarter after a reaffirmation.
findings.independence: H1 EBITDA from the Q1 release https://ir.nayax.com/news/news-details/2026/Nayax-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx and the Q2 6-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001901279/000117891326003978/exhibit_99-1.htm . FY2025 EBITDA from https://ir.nayax.com/news/news-details/2026/Nayax-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx . Against this: management guided adj. opex to ~$42m a quarter with hardware margin back to Q1 levels in H2, which roughly reaches the low end of the range.

findings.finding: Organic growth slowed from 26% (Q1) to 21.4% (Q2). The ~$134m Q3 consensus needs ~22% organic on the $104.3m Q3 2025 base. Management said H2 is ~55% of the year, which implies H2 of $280-290m and Q4 of ~$146-156m excluding IPS. The reported-quarter revenue bar therefore sits inside the guided path and is not a stretch.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue of $122.6m (+28%) was in line or a beat and the stock still fell 10% on the cash guide. Q1 2026 +32% revenue with an EPS miss went +3.3% on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the deceleration is in the wire copy and the sweep lists it as known. What is not visible is whether Q3 organic growth holds at ~21% or slips below 20%, which would put the 22-25% FY organic range in doubt. A slight negative lean because the trend is downward.

But a founder-CEO buying ~$9m near quarter-end, just after closing a $350m deal, is information about the quarter the market only gets to check tomorrow. If it were fully priced, the stock would not still be 36% below its high.

findings.finding: Q2 free cash flow was -$13.1m and FCF conversion guidance was cut to 5-10% of adj. EBITDA on accelerated spend (financial services including the Nayax America Bank application, Lynkwell EV charging, component sourcing). IPS was then funded with ~$200m of cash plus ~$150m of new Israeli bank debt, taking net leverage to ~3.8x at close (stated target below 3x by end-2027). Q3 cash flow and the post-close balance sheet are new numbers in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FCF guide cut on 2026-08-10 drove -10.2% on day one and about -28% over three sessions.
findings.why_not_priced: Lesson 4 answer: the money buys an asset the company says is accretive with ~80% FCF conversion, plus growth spend. It is not distress, and weak Q3 cash would land inside the 5-10% guide. Kept as a small negative only because this shareholder base sold hard on cash last time, and a further cut to the conversion guide or a wider burn would hit the same nerve.
findings.independence: Leverage and financing from deal coverage https://capital.com/en-ke/news/nayax-completes-acquisition-of-ips-group ; KBW called the August drop an overreaction (Globes https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-1001552414 ).

findings.finding: July 2026 security incident: a subsidiary's cloud account was breached, and the company confirmed that backup documents and transaction records were exfiltrated (no sensitive authentication data). Attackers claimed 100TB and threatened publication. Q3 carries incident-response costs, and the call may bring questions on customer churn or card-network scrutiny.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 8.3% on Nasdaq on the 2026-07-07 disclosure.
findings.why_not_priced: The event is priced. Any cost or customer effect has not been quantified in public. This is a below-the-line one-off unless it shows up in churn or the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.

findings.finding: The shekel has held at multi-decade highs (USD/ILS below 3.0 in 2026). That raises the dollar cost of Nayax's Israeli R&D and G&A base while it reports in USD. This is a macro proxy that the company has not confirmed for Q3.

findings.why_not_priced: Known macro, and the August reaffirmation was made with the shekel already strong, so this is largely priced. Filed small as an unconfirmed proxy.

findings.why_not_priced: Public and small. It matters only if management puts numbers on these channels in the outlook.

findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the thing to beat, not an edge in itself. Sized small: with no crowded short there is no squeeze mechanism, only a low bar.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The mild negative lean (H2 EBITDA ramp, cash sensitivity) cuts against a +10.75% 20-day run-up that coincides with CEO buying, so the evidence roughly offsets and p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the IPS debt buys an asset the company calls accretive with ~80% FCF conversion, and a weak Q3 FCF lands inside the 5-10% guide, so the financing finding moved from -0.5 to -0.3.
Partly-priced positioning: the CEO buying is public and the stock has already risen ~10% since, so it moved from +0.8 to +0.6.
Lesson on untrustworthy FPI histories: confirms the rebuilt reaction base; abs_move_pct unchanged at 6.0.
Lessons 5 and 7 left the proxy (shekel) and the positioning findings standing as filed; the post-lessons sum equals the pre-lessons sum (-1.1) because the two changes offset.
